title: Take a user offline when their last connection closes

blocks.text: The chat service shows a green dot next to everyone who is online. A user counts as online while at least one of their connections (phone, laptop, another tab) is open. Connection events arrive on many threads at once, and the gateway sometimes sends a disconnect twice, or for a user it never reported as connected.

`Presence` keeps an open-connection count per user in a `ConcurrentHashMap`, and `online()` lists the users that have an entry. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Presence.java`: `connect(user)` and `disconnect(user)`, each one call on the map. When you're done, a user whose last connection closes disappears from `online()`, and a disconnect nobody can match leaves the map as it was. About two lines in total.

cases.says: connections are counted per user, and a user with an open connection stays online
when the last connection closes the user's entry goes, so they are no longer online
a disconnect for a user with no open connection adds nothing to the map

origin.section: A Remapping Function That Returns null Removes the Entry

concepts: Map.merge stores the given value for an absent key without calling the function.
A remapping function given to compute, computeIfPresent or merge removes the entry when it returns null; returning the old value leaves the entry as it is.
